title: Handover of a deteriorating patient to the night team

header.contentArea: Communication skills in giving and receiving information and history taking

related.why: The same structure when you need a senior now
Fluids, AKI and the emergency laparotomy patient

brief.scenario: Mr Peter Hollis, 72, 80 kg, is day 1 after an emergency laparotomy and small bowel resection for a strangulated incisional hernia. At 2 pm his NEWS2 was 1. You saw him at 7 pm, gave a 500 ml crystalloid bolus at 7.15 pm and sent bloods. At 7.30 pm: RR 22, SpO2 95% on air, BP 104/68, pulse 108, alert, temperature 37.8°C. Urine output over the last 3 hours: 25, 20 and 15 ml. Venous lactate 2.1 mmol/L; FBC and U&E are pending.
brief.task: Hand over Mr Hollis to the night surgical registrar (the examiner).

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Sickest first, SBAR, a timed jobs list, clear "call if" triggers, resuscitation status, read-back.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: "He's a bit dry, keep an eye on him": no score, no times, no triggers.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Work out NEWS2 before you start, and lead with it.

grid.label: Situation
grid.fail: Starts with a chronological story; gives no score or concern.
grid.pass: Names the patient, ward, bed and consultant, and the concern: NEWS2 5, up from 1, with falling urine output.
grid.high: Hands him over first as the sickest patient, and checks the registrar has the handover list in front of them.

grid.label: Background
grid.fail: Omits the operation, the day, or relevant history.
grid.pass: Age and weight, day 1 after emergency laparotomy and small bowel resection; relevant history and allergies.
grid.high: Adds what changes decisions tonight: the anastomosis, preoperative haemoglobin and the time of the last enoxaparin dose.

grid.label: Assessment
grid.fail: Reads out observations without interpreting them.
grid.pass: Interprets: NEWS2 5 is the key threshold for an urgent response; he is oliguric; hypovolaemia, bleeding or early sepsis.
grid.high: Gives the response to treatment so far, a working diagnosis, and the next investigation if he doesn't respond.

grid.label: Jobs list with priorities and times
grid.fail: Vague jobs ("keep an eye on him") with no times or owner.
grid.pass: Timed jobs: a further bolus now, as he hasn't responded to the first; at least hourly observations and urine output; review at 8.30 pm; chase the bloods.
grid.high: Says who does each job, and the next step if he still hasn't responded: repeat lactate, senior review, consider CT.

grid.label: Escalation triggers (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Gives no thresholds for calling for help.
grid.borderline: Says "call me if he gets worse" without defining worse.
grid.pass: Call if NEWS2 reaches 7 or more, any single parameter scores 3 (e.g. systolic 90 or less), or urine stays low after fluid.
grid.high: Links each trigger to an action: NEWS2 7 or more means an emergency response, critical care outreach and the consultant told.

grid.label: Ceiling of care and resuscitation status
grid.fail: Doesn't know his resuscitation status or ceiling of care.
grid.pass: States he is for full escalation, including critical care, and for CPR, as documented by the consultant.
grid.high: Says where it is documented, that his wife knows, and that the consultant wants a call if he deteriorates.

grid.label: Two-way handover and read-back
grid.fail: Leaves without checking the plan was understood.
grid.pass: Invites questions; asks the registrar to read back the jobs and triggers, and corrects any error.
grid.high: States that responsibility now passes to the registrar, and tells the nurse in charge the plan and triggers.

grid.label: Documentation
grid.pass: Written handover on the list or proforma; plan and triggers documented in the notes.
grid.high: Records the handover time and the receiving doctor, and rates him red on the list (unstable, diagnosis unclear).

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Can I start with the sickest? Mr Hollis, Ward 9, bed 12, under Mr Hale. Have you got the list? I'm worried about him: NEWS2 5, up from 1 at 2 pm, and falling urine output.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: He's 72, 80 kg, day 1 after emergency laparotomy and small bowel resection with an anastomosis, for a strangulated incisional hernia. Preoperative haemoglobin 132. Enoxaparin given at 6 pm. No allergies.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: At 7.30: RR 22, sats 95% on air, BP 104/68, pulse 108, alert, 37.8: NEWS2 5, the urgent-response threshold. Urine 25, 20, 15 ml an hour; at 80 kg he should make at least 40. No real response yet to 500 ml at 7.15. Most likely he's dry; bleeding and an early leak are the worries. Lactate 2.1; Hb and creatinine pending. If he doesn't respond, I think he needs a CT.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Jobs, in order: I've prescribed a second 500 ml bolus, going up now. The nurse does obs and urine hourly. You review him at 8.30. If he's no better: repeat lactate, a senior look and consider CT. I've asked the lab to phone the Hb; if it has dropped, hold his next enoxaparin and call Mr Hale.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Triggers: NEWS2 7 or more is an emergency response: outreach now, and Mr Hale told. Systolic 90 or less scores 3 on its own. Urine under 40 an hour for more than 6 hours would meet the AKI definition.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: He's for full escalation, including ICU, and for CPR. Mr Hale documented it on the ward round, his wife knows, and he wants a call if Mr Hollis deteriorates.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Any questions? Could you read back the jobs and triggers? [Corrects one error] From now he's yours; I'll tell the nurse in charge the plan and triggers.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: He's red on the list, with the time and your name, and the plan is in his notes.

failures.move: "Call if he gets worse" with no defined triggers.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: nobody knows when to escalate, so deterioration is recognised late.

failures.move: Reading out observations without the NEWS2 or the trend.
failures.consequence: The registrar can't prioritise him against other patients.
In an arrest, the night team has to make the decision with no information.
Errors in the plan, like the wrong trigger, go uncorrected.

recovery.line: Sorry, the headline: Mr Hollis has a NEWS2 of 5, up from 1, and falling urine output. He needs review at 8.30.

recovery.when: You don't know his resuscitation status
recovery.line: I'll check it in the notes now and tell you before I leave.

knowledge.fact: NEWS2 5–6: key threshold for urgent response, at least hourly observations. Single parameter 3: urgent ward-based response. 7 or more: emergency response, registrar informed, critical care team, continuous monitoring.
Oliguria: under 0.5 ml/kg/h; AKI if it lasts more than 6 hours (1.3.1).
Resuscitation bolus: 500 ml crystalloid over less than 15 minutes (1.3.1); for suspected sepsis, follow the NICE sepsis guideline (1.3.2).
Handover minimum: name, age, location, consultant, diagnosis, results; add review urgency, a "what if" plan, resuscitation plan and outstanding tasks.
Across five handovers, 2.5% of information survives with no written record; 99% with a standardised proforma.

If infection is suspected, NEWS2 5–6 is medium risk: venous gas with lactate, blood cultures, FBC, CRP, U&E; FY2-or-above review within 1 hour; antibiotic decision within 3 hours. Sepsis fluids: 250 ml boluses, reassess after each, senior advice after 1,000 ml.

recall.think: Early deterioration on day 1: hypovolaemia, bleeding or a leak.
recall.say: "I'm worried about Mr Hollis: NEWS2 5, up from 1, and falling urine output."
do: Resuscitation status, read-back, write it down

numbers.meaning: NEWS2 key threshold for urgent response

recall.finish: Named review at 8.30 pm; senior and CT if no response.

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format; introduce yourself at every station

sources.name: NHS England and NHS Improvement: SBAR communication tool – situation, background, assessment, recommendation (Online library of Quality, Service Improvement and Redesign tools)
sources.supports: SBAR structure; state the concern and early warning score first; be specific about the request and time frame; advice given by phone is repeated back; agreed recommendations are documented in the notes

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2
sources.supports: Parameter bands (Chart 1); aggregate 5–6: key threshold for urgent response; single parameter 3: urgent ward-based response; 7 or more: urgent or emergency response (Chart 2); 5 or more: at least hourly monitoring and urgent assessment; 7 or more: inform medical team at least at specialist registrar level, emergency assessment by a team with critical care competencies, continuous monitoring (Chart 4)

sources.name: Royal College of Surgeons of England: Safe handover: guidance from the Working Time Directive working party
sources.supports: Minimum information: patient name and age, date of admission, location, responsible consultant, current diagnosis, results of significant or pending investigations; also condition, urgency and frequency of review, management plan including 'what if…', resuscitation plan, consultant contact details, outstanding tasks; more extensive information on patients who are particularly unwell; assign tasks and responsibilities clearly; handover is a two-way process

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: Acute care toolkit 1: Handover
sources.supports: Define who is relinquishing responsibility and who is now responsible, including specific tasks; standardise communication (e.g. SBAR), with repetition so that understanding is shared; standardised documentation; red–amber–green risk rating (red: haemodynamic or respiratory instability, unclear diagnosis, sepsis); over five handovers, 2.5% of information is retained with no written record, 85.5% with notes and 99% with a standardised proforma (Bhabra et al. 2007)

sources.name: NICE NG148: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
sources.supports: Oliguria: urine output less than 0.5 ml/kg/hour; systems to recognise and respond to oliguria in adults at risk (1.2.2); detect AKI by a fall in urine output to less than 0.5 ml/kg/hour for more than 6 hours in adults, or a creatinine rise of 26 micromol/litre or more within 48 hours, or a 50% rise within 7 days (1.3.1)

sources.name: NICE CG174: Intravenous fluid therapy in adults in hospital
sources.supports: Resuscitation: crystalloid with sodium 130–154 mmol/l, 500 ml bolus over less than 15 minutes (1.3.1); for suspected sepsis, follow the NICE sepsis guidelines (1.3.2)

sources.name: NICE NG253: Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management
sources.supports: Medium risk: suspected infection and NEWS2 5–6; bloods including lactate and cultures, FY2+ review within 1 hour (1.8.16); antibiotics may be deferred up to 3 hours (1.8.17); 250 ml boluses up to 1,000 ml, reassess after each, senior advice after 1,000 ml (1.8.6–1.8.9)

media.task: Read the observation trend and calculate NEWS2 before handing over
media.description: A NEWS2 observation chart for Mr Hollis showing 2 pm (RR 18, SpO2 96% on air, BP 122/74, pulse 92, alert, 37.4°C; NEWS2 1) and 7.30 pm (RR 22, SpO2 95% on air, BP 104/68, pulse 108, alert, 37.8°C; NEWS2 5), with a fluid balance chart showing hourly urine 25, 20 and 15 ml

partner.opening: You're handing over to the night registrar. Please begin when you're ready.
partner.actorBrief: You are the night surgical registrar, starting your shift with a list of 20 patients. Opening line: "Right, who's first?" Emotional state: friendly but pressed for time. If the candidate hasn't told you why Mr Hollis matters within about 30 seconds, interrupt: "Is there anyone you're worried about?" Ask "What's his NEWS2?", "Is he for escalation?" and "What do you want me to do?" if they are not offered. When asked to read back, make one deliberate error: "Call outreach if NEWS2 goes above 7." Accept a correction. If the candidate doesn't ask for a read-back, don't give one. If asked who will review at 8.30 pm, say you may be in theatre (see curveball).

reveals.trigger: Asks the registrar to read back
reveals.finding: "Review at 8.30, chase bloods, hourly obs. Call outreach if NEWS2 goes above 7." (deliberate error)

reveals.trigger: Asks if the registrar has questions
reveals.finding: "When was his last enoxaparin, and what was his Hb before surgery?"

push.question: What NEWS2 score needs an emergency response, and what does that involve?
push.expect: 7 or more: registrar-level review at least, emergency assessment by a team with critical care competencies, continuous monitoring, and consider level 2 or 3 care.

curveballs.prompt: "I'll be in theatre at 8.30. Can the F1 review him?"
curveballs.safeAnswer: Only with the triggers and a named senior to call; otherwise ask critical care outreach to review; someone named must own the 8.30 pm review.

curveballs.prompt: "NEWS2 of 5 on day 1 after a laparotomy is normal, isn't it?"
curveballs.safeAnswer: Disagree: 5 is the key threshold for urgent response, with at least hourly observations, whatever the day.
No: for CPR and full escalation, documented by the consultant today.
